en: Opposite in effect, nature or order.
Reverse, opposite in order.
An inverted state: a state in which something has been turned (properly) upside down or (loosely) inside out or backwards.
The reverse of any procedure or process.
To compute the bearing and distance between two points.

inverse.ety: Recorded since 1440, from Latin inversus, the past participle of invertere (“to invert”), itself from in- (“against, in”) + vertere (“to turn”).

note.ja: in（反対に）+ vers（向ける）+ e。向きを反対にした →「逆の・反対の」。

en: Having the order or direction exchanged; for example, turned upside down, reversed, or in any other way opposite or contrary and swapped.
Having the lowest note transposed an octave higher.

ex.en: Through the lens the image was inverted.
ex.ja: レンズを通ると像は逆になった。

ex.en: Place your skis in an inverted V.
ex.ja: あなたのスキーを逆Ｖ字型にしなさい。

note.ja: invert（逆にする）+ -ed。in + vertere（回す）。「逆さの」。inverted commas（引用符）。

en: The act of irritating or annoying.
The state of being irritated.

irritation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French irritation, from Latin irrītātiō, from irrītāre (“to excite”). By surface analysis, irritate + -ion.

ex.en: There was no irritation on his part.
ex.ja: 彼としては少しもいらいらしてなかった。

ex.en: Her mood graduated to irritation.
ex.ja: 彼女の気分は次第にいら立ちはじめた。

note.ja: irritate（いらだたせる）+ -ion。ラテン語 irritare（刺激する）。「いらだち・炎症」。

en: Any word used as the key to a code.
Any word used in a reference work to link to other words or other information.
To tag with keywords, as for example to facilitate searching.

note.ja: key（鍵・重要な）+ word（語）。「キーワード」。

en: Expending or bestowing profusely; profuse; prodigal.
Superabundant; excessive.
To give out extremely generously; to squander.
To give out to (somebody) extremely generously.

lavish.ety: From Middle English laves, lavas, lavage (“extravagant, wasteful, prodigal”), from lavas (“excessive abundance”), from Old French lavasse, lavache (“torrent of rain”); possibly later conflated in some senses by Middle English laven (“to pour out”), equivalent to lave + -ish. Compare Scots lawage, lavisch, lavish (“unrestrained, excessively prodigal, extravagant”). Compare also English lavy (“lavish, liberal”), Dutch lafenis (“lavishness”).

ex.en: He is lavish with his money.
ex.ja: 彼は金を惜しみなく使う。

ex.en: He's lavish with his money.
ex.ja: 彼は金を惜しみなく使う。

ex.en: The real estate broker was lavish in his spending in Ginza.
ex.ja: その不動産屋は銀座で気前よく金を使った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 lavasse（どしゃ降り）から。laver（洗う）。「惜しみない・ぜいたくな」。

en: A means of providing the necessities of life for oneself (for example, a job or income).

livelihood.ety: From Middle English liflode, from Old English līflād (“course of life, conduct”), from līf (“life”) + lād (“course, journey”), later altered under the influence of lively, -hood. Compare life, lode.

ex.en: How is livelihood in America these day?
ex.ja: 最近のアメリカ人の暮らし振りはどうですか。

ex.en: Life and livelihood are the same thing.
ex.ja: 金と命は同義語だよ。

ex.en: The ordinary people had their livelihood in farming rice.
ex.ja: 庶民のなりわいは、米をつくることだった。

note.ja: 古英語 līflād（人生の道）から。life + lode（道）。のちに likelihood の影響を受けた。「生計」。

en: Of or pertaining to medicines; medical.
A physician.
A paramedic, someone with special training in first aid, especially in the military.

medic.ety: Borrowed from Latin medicus m (“of or belonging to healing, curative, medical; as a noun, medicus, masculine, a physician, doctor, surgeon”), Late Latin medica f (“a female physician, midwife”), from mederi (“to heal”).

note.ja: ラテン語 medicus（医者）から。medical、medicine と同じ。

en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.
Having diverse characteristics, abilities or appearances.

miscellaneous.ety: Borrowed from Latin miscellāneus, from miscellus (“mixed”), from misceō (“mix”).

ex.en: I keep all my miscellaneous files in this folder.
ex.ja: このフォルダーに、「その他」に分類される全てのファイルを入れて保管しています。

ex.en: That drawer is full of miscellaneous items.
ex.ja: あの引き出しの中は雑多なもので溢れかえっている。

note.ja: ラテン語 miscellaneus（混ぜた）から。miscere（混ぜる）。「種々雑多な」。mix と同じ。

Of a plan, policy, etc.: not properly planned or thought through; ill-conceived.

en: An assemblage or display; a gathering, collection of people or things.
An assembling or review of troops, as for parade, verification of numbers, inspection, exercise, or introduction into service.
To be gathered together for parade, inspection, exercise, or the like (especially of a military force); to come together as parts of a fo…
To collect, call or assemble together, such as troops or a group for inspection, orders, display etc.

muster.ety: From Middle English musteren, borrowed from Anglo-Norman mostrer, Middle French monstrer, moustrer (whence the noun monstre, which gave the English noun), from Latin mōnstrō (“to show”), from moneō (“to admonish”). Cognate with French montrer (“to show”), Italian mostrare (“to show”), Spanish mostrar (“to show”). See also monster.

ex.en: I mustered up my courage and went there.
ex.ja: 私は思い切ってそこに行った。

ex.en: I'm sure it'll work out, so muster your courage!
ex.ja: きっとうまく行くから、勇気を出せ！

ex.en: She finally mustered up the courage to ask him for more money.
ex.ja: 彼女はついに勇気を出して彼の借金の申し込みをした。

note.ja: ラテン語 monstrare（示す）から。「（兵を）集めて見せる」→「召集する・奮い起こす」。demonstrate と同じ。

en: A string or flat strip of pasta or other dough, usually cooked (at least initially) by boiling, and served in soup or in a dry form mixed…
An object which is long and thin like a noodle (sense 1).
To hum or sing (a tune) at a low pitch or volume.

noodle.ety:
Borrowed from Dutch noedel (“noodle”), or from its etymon German Nudel (“piece of pasta, noodle”); further etymology uncertain, probably a variant of Knödel (“dumpling”), from Middle High German knödel (“dumpling; small knot”), and then either:
* from knode, knote (“knot”) (from Old High German knodo, knoto (“knot”), perhaps ultimately related to Proto-West Germanic *knappō (“knob; boy”)) + -el (diminutive suffix); or
* from Ladin menùdli (“small dough dumpling in soup”), probably from Latin minutulus (“very small, tiny”) (in the sense of food chopped into small pieces), a diminutive of minūtu

ex.en: You're right. The noodle broth here is a bit expensive.
ex.ja: その通りさ。ここの麺の出汁はちょっと値が張るんだ。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Nudel から。「麺」→（俗）「頭」。

en: Originally, the DuPont company trade name for polyamide, a copolymer whose molecules consist of alternating diamine and dicarboxylic acid…
A stocking originally fabricated from nylon; also used generically for any long, sheer stocking worn on a woman's legs.

nylon.ety: Coined by the company DuPont in 1938. According to the company, the name was formed from the random generic syllable nyl- + the common fiber suffix -on (as in rayon and Dacron), said to be ultimately from cotton.

ex.en: These nylon socks wash well.
ex.ja: このナイロンソックスは、洗濯がきく。

ex.en: Nylon stockings often run.
ex.ja: ナイロンストッキングはすぐ伝線する。

note.ja: 1938年にデュポン社が作った合成繊維の名。語源ははっきりしない。

en: To ride across or beyond something.
To ride over the top of something, usually forcibly.
A mechanism, device or procedure used to counteract an automatic control.
A royalty.

override.ety: From Middle English overriden, from Old English oferrīdan, equivalent to over- + ride. Cognate with Dutch overrijden, German überreiten, Danish override.

ex.en: The President vetoed the bill, but Congress overrode his veto.
ex.ja: 大統領はその法案に対して拒否権を行使しましたが、議会が再度それを無効にしました。

ex.en: Under the Constitution, the lower chamber's resolutions override those of the upper chamber.
ex.ja: 憲法の規定に従い衆院の議決が参院に優越する。

note.ja: over（上を）+ ride（乗る）。「上を乗り越える」→「覆す・優先する」。

en: An allotrope of oxygen (symbol O₃) having three atoms in the molecule instead of the usual two; it is a toxic gas, generated from oxygen …
Fresh air, especially that breathed at the seaside and smelling of seaweed.
To treat with ozone.

ozone.ety:
From German Ozon, coined 1840 by Christian Friedrich Schönbein, from Ancient Greek ὄζον (ózon), neuter participle of ὄζω (ózō, “I smell”), in reference to its pungent odour.
The “fresh air” sense is from an erroneous former belief that seaweed contains and releases ozone.

ex.en: Without the ozone layer, we would be in danger.
ex.ja: もしオゾン層がなければ、私たちは危機に直面しているだろう。

ex.en: The ozone layer continues to be further destroyed every year.
ex.ja: オゾン層は年々破壊が進んでいる。

ex.en: This chart illustrates the function of ozone layer.
ex.ja: この図はオゾン層の機能を説明している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ozein（におう）から。独特のにおいから「オゾン」。

en: Extreme, irrational distrust of others.

paranoia.ety:
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek παράνοια (paránoia, “madness”), from παράνοος (paránoos, “demented”), from παρά (pará, “beyond, beside”) + νόος (nóos, “mind, spirit”).
By surface analysis, para- (“abnormal, beyond”) + nous (“mind”) + -ia (“(medical) condition”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paranoia ＝ para（外れて）+ nous（心）。「心が外れること」→「被害妄想」。

en: The hard durable surface placed directly atop the ground, as on a street or sidewalk.
Interior pavement, as in a cathedral.
Pertaining to the material used for pavement, or to the surface itself.

note.ja: pave（舗装する）+ -ing。ラテン語 pavire（突き固める）。pavement と同じ。

en: To pursue in a manner to do harm or cruelty to; especially, because of the victim's race, sexual identity, or adherence to a particular b…
To harass with importunity; to pursue with persistent solicitations; to annoy.

persecute.ety: Borrowed from Middle French persécuter, from Ecclesiastical Latin persecutor, from Latin persequor, persecutus (“follow up, pursue”), from per- (“through”) + sequor (“follow”) (English sequel). Compare prosecute. Cf. also pursue.

ex.en: He persecuted people for their religion.
ex.ja: 彼は人々を宗教により迫害しました。

ex.en: Some early religion's leaders were persecuted by their enemies.
ex.ja: 初期の宗教指導者の中には敵対する人々に迫害されたものもいる。

ex.en: The Romans persecuted Christians.
ex.ja: ローマ人はキリスト教徒を迫害した。

note.ja: per（どこまでも）+ secu（追う）+ te。しつこく追い回す →「迫害する」。prosecute（起訴する）と混同注意。

en: A person from Peru or of Peruvian descent.
Of, from, or pertaining to Peru or the Peruvian people.

Peruvian.ety: From Peru + -v- + -ian, or from Latin Peruvia.

note.ja: Peru + -vian。「ペルーの」。

en: A person whose occupation specializes in the science of physics, especially at a professional level.

physicist.ety: From physics + -ist. Coined by the English polymath William Whewell (1794–1866) in his book The Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences (1840): see the quotation.

ex.en: He is as great a physicist as ever lived.
ex.ja: 彼はいまだかつてないぐらい偉大な物理学者である。

ex.en: He is a physicist.
ex.ja: 彼は物理学者だ。

ex.en: He's a famous physicist not only in Japan, but throughout the world.
ex.ja: 彼は日本のみならず、世界においても有名な物理学者である。

note.ja: physics（物理学）+ -ist。ギリシャ語 physis（自然）。「物理学者」。

en: The state of being plural.
The holding of multiple benefices.

plurality.ety: From plural + -ity, from Middle English pluralite, from Old French pluralité (“multitude, state of being plural”), from Latin plūrālitās.

note.ja: plural（複数の）+ -ity。ラテン語 plus（より多く）。「多数・複数性」→ 選挙の「相対多数」。

en: Of or relating to the epoch before written record.
Ancient; very old, outdated, etc.

prehistoric.ety: From pre- (“before”) + historic, q.v., similar to slightly earlier ante-historic.

note.ja: pre（前の）+ historic（歴史の）。「有史以前の」。

en: A part of speech that refers anaphorically to a noun or noun phrase, which cannot ordinarily be preceded by a determiner and rarely takes…
Any of the third-person pronouns by which a person prefers to be referred to, typically reflecting their gender identity; often communica…

pronoun.ety: From pro- + noun, modeled on Middle French pronom, from Latin pronomen, itself a calque of Ancient Greek ᾰ̓ντωνῠμῐ́ᾱ (ăntōnŭmĭ́ā).

ex.en: I don't know why the English pronoun "I" always appears with a capital letter.
ex.ja: なんで英語の代名詞"I"はいつも大文字表記なのかわからない。

ex.en: Relative pronouns perform as 'conjunction + pronoun'.
ex.ja: 関係代名詞は「接続詞+代名詞」のはたらきをしています。

ex.en: One of the greatest hurdles facing middle school students learning English is relative pronouns.
ex.ja: 中学生が英語を学ぶ際の最難関の一つが関係代名詞です。

note.ja: pro（代わりに）+ noun（名詞）。「名詞の代わり」→「代名詞」。

The atomic nucleus of protium (hydrogen-1)

The human mind as the central force in thought, emotion, and behavior of an individual.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 psyche（息・魂）から。→「精神・心・魂」。psychology（心理学）。

ex.ja: 彼は誤りを認めるのを嫌がらない。

en: The process by which an object, person, place or idea may be copied mimicked or reproduced.
Copy; reproduction.

replication.ety: Inherited from Middle English replicacioun, replicacion, from Anglo-Norman replicacioun and Old French replicacion (“reply, answer”), from Latin replicātiō, replicātiōnem. By surface analysis, replicate + -(at)ion.

note.ja: replicate（複製する）+ -ion。「複製・再現」→ 実験の「追試」。

en: A rotating part of a mechanical device; for example, in an electric motor, generator, alternator, or pump.
In a disc brake, the metal disc attached to the wheel hub.

rotor.ety: From an irregular clipping of rotator, originally in mathematics, coined by English mathematician and philosopher William Kingdon Clifford based on vector, see quotations. Doublet of rota and ruote.

To deposit material as a sediment.
To be deposited as a sediment.

en: Aloneness; the state of being alone, solitary, or by oneself.
A lonely or deserted place.

solitude.ety: From Middle English solitude, from Old French solitude, from Latin sōlitūdō. By surface analysis, sole + -itude.

ex.en: He likes to spend some time in solitude every day.
ex.ja: 彼は毎日好んで独りで過ごす時間を持つ。

ex.en: Some people enjoy solitude.
ex.ja: 孤独を楽しむ人もいる。

ex.en: I like to go to a cabin in the woods to enjoy solitude.
ex.ja: 私は孤独を楽しむために森の小屋に行くのが好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 solitudo（孤独）から。solus（ひとりの）。solitary、solo と同じ。

en: A state of readiness without immediate involvement; remaining in preparation for (a sudden or unforeseen event or situation).
A replacement kept on standby.

ex.en: Just my old standby: lemon chicken.
ex.ja: 私の十八番、チキンのレモン煮よ。

note.ja: stand by（そばに控える）の名詞化。「待機・予備」。

en: A place built to withstand attack; a fortress.
A place of domination by, or refuge or survival of, a particular group or idea.

stronghold.ety: From Middle English stranghalde, strong-hold, strong-holde, from strong (“having physical strength, sturdy, strong; built to withstand assaults, fortified”) (from Old English strang, strong (“strong”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *strengʰ- (“stiff, tight”)) + hōld (“grasp, grip; control, possession, rule”) (from Old English). By surface analysis, strong + hold.

ex.en: That village is the enemy's last stronghold.
ex.ja: あの村が敵の最後の牙城です。

note.ja: strong（強い）+ hold（とりで）。「とりで」→「拠点」。

note.ja: theory + -ist。「理論家」。

therein.ety: From Middle English theryn, ther-inne, þer-in, from Old English þǣrin, þǣrinne, from Proto-West Germanic *þārin, *þārinna, from Proto-Germanic *þarin, *þarinna, equivalent to there + in. Cognate with Saterland Frisian deerin (“therein”), West Frisian dêryn (“therein”), Dutch daarin (“therein”), German Low German daarin (“therein”), German darin, drin (“therein”), Danish deri (“therein”), Swedish däri (“therein”), Icelandic þar í (“therein”).

ex.en: Therein lies the problem.
ex.ja: そこに問題がある。

note.ja: there + in。「そこに」。法律文で使う硬い言い方。

en: Shaped like a triangle.
Of, or pertaining to, triangles.

triangular.ety: From Middle English triangulare, trianguler, triangulere, from Old French triangulaire, triangulier and Latin triangulāris. By surface analysis, tri- + -angular.

note.ja: triangle + -ar。「三角形の」。

en: A soldier of private rank in cavalry or armor.
A cavalry horse; a charger.
To work as a trooper.
To work steadily at an unpleasant job without complaint.

trooper.ety: From troop + -er, from French troupe. The sense of “one who endures adversity” comes from trouper (“member of an acting troupe”) but through assimilation with the sense of “soldier” has come to be usually spelled “trooper”.

note.ja: troop（隊）+ -er。「騎兵」→（米）「州警察官」。

en: Honest, and always telling the truth.
Accurately depicting what is real.

truthful.ety: From truth + -ful. Piecewise doublet of trothful, from Middle English trouþeful.

ex.en: She brought up her children to be truthful.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供を正直であるように育てた。

ex.en: I don't think he is truthful.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことは本当ではないと思う。

ex.en: His report was truthful.
ex.ja: 彼の報告は真実だった。

note.ja: truth（真実）+ -ful。「正直な」。

en: A little tower, frequently a merely ornamental structure at one of the corners of a building or castle.
A siege tower; a movable building, of a square form, consisting of ten or even twenty stories and sometimes one hundred and twenty cubits…

turret.ety: From Middle English touret, from Old French torete (French tourette), diminutive of tour (“tower”), from Latin turris. Doublet of tor, tourelle, and tower. See tower.

note.ja: 古フランス語 tourete（小さな塔）から。tour（塔）。tower と同じ。

zh: 無處不在的 /无处不在的
無所不在的 /无所不在的

en: Being everywhere at once: omnipresent.
Appearing to be everywhere at once; being or seeming to be in more than one location at the same time.

ubiquitous.ety: From ubiquity + -ous, from Medieval Latin ubīquitās, from Latin ubīque (“everywhere”), from ubī̆ (“where”) + -que (“each, ever”). Compare ubiety.

note.ja: ラテン語 ubique（どこにでも）から。ubi（どこに）。「どこにでもある」。

en: In a manner that one does not or cannot believe.
To an extent not to be believed.

ex.en: The result was unbelievably good.
ex.ja: 結果は信じられないほど良かった。

ex.en: The results were unbelievably good.
ex.ja: 結果は信じられないほど良かった。

note.ja: unbelievable + -ly。「信じられないほど」。

Out of the ordinary.

ex.ja: スラングやフランクな会話、独特な短縮語尾まで含めた例文が必要です。

note.ja: un（否定）+ conventional（慣例の）。「型破りな」。convention と同じ。

en: In an unnecessary way; not by necessity.
To an extent beyond what is needed.

ex.en: The manager was unnecessarily rough on him.
ex.ja: 支配人は必要以上に彼につらく当たった。

ex.en: There is no need to be unnecessarily anxious about the outbreak.
ex.ja: その突発について不必要に心配する必要はない。

note.ja: unnecessary + -ly。「不必要に」。

ex.en: His immoral actions did not go unnoticed.
ex.ja: 彼のふしだらな行為は気付かれずにはすまなかった。

ex.en: In a town you may pass unnoticed, whereas in a village it's impossible.
ex.ja: 都会では気付かれず通り過ぎることもあるだろうが、村の中ではそうはいかない。

note.ja: un（否定）+ noticed（気づかれた）。「気づかれない」。

Not eaten.

The spiritual beliefs of the Ewe/Fon of West Africa, practiced chiefly in Benin and in the south of Togo.
To bewitch someone or something using voodoo

ex.en: I don't believe in voodoo.
ex.ja: ブードゥー教は信じていません。

ex.ja: ブードゥー教の信者ではありません。

note.ja: 西アフリカのエウェ語 vodu（精霊）から。「ブードゥー教」。

en: The practice of witches; magic, sorcery, or the use of supernatural powers to influence or predict events.
Black magic; the use of witchcraft for evil means.

witchcraft.ety: From Middle English wicchecraft, wicchecreft, from Old English wiċċecræft, equivalent to witch + -craft.

ex.en: This is not witchcraft.
ex.ja: これは魔法ではありません。

note.ja: witch（魔女）+ craft（技）。「魔術」。

en: Sexual intercourse by a married person with someone other than their spouse. See more synonyms at Thesaurus:cuckoldry
Lewdness or unchastity of thought as well as act, as forbidden by the sixth/seventh commandment; sinful sexual behavior as a category.

adultery.ety: With change of suffix, from the Old French adultere (“violation of conjugal faith”) (in Bernard of Clairvaux, Sermons, 12c.), a learnèd borrowing from Latin adulterium, from adulterō. Replaced the older form avoutrie, from the inherited Old French forms avouterie or aoulterie, while keeping its suffix. Compare French adultère (“adultery”). Displaced Old English ǣwbryċe. Not related to adult.

ex.en: According to many religions, adultery is a crime.
ex.ja: 多くの宗教において、姦淫は罪悪とされる。

ex.en: The crime of adultery was abolished in 1947.
ex.ja: 昭和２２年に姦通罪は廃止されました。

note.ja: ラテン語 adulterare（混ぜ物をする・汚す）から。adulterate（混ぜ物をする）と同じ。「不倫」。adult とは別語源。

en: Having the faculty of quick motion in the limbs; apt or ready to move; loose-jointed.
Characterised by quick motion.
Agile software development.

agile.ety: From earlier agil, borrowed from Latin agilis (“agile, nimble”), from agō (“do, act; move”). See agent.

ex.en: This athlete is strong and agile.
ex.ja: このアスリートは、力もあるし機敏だ。

note.ja: ag（動かす・行う）+ ile。すばやく動ける →「機敏な・身軽な」。

en: In an anonymous manner; without a name.
In an anonymous manner; without individuality.

anonymously.ety:
Etymology tree
English anonymous
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English anonymously
From anonymous + -ly.

ex.en: He anonymously donated a large sum of money to the Red Cross.
ex.ja: 彼は匿名で赤十字に多額のお金を寄付した。

note.ja: anonymous + -ly。ギリシャ語 an（否定）+ onyma（名）。「匿名で」。

en: Severity of manners or life; extreme rigor or strictness; harsh discipline.
Freedom from adornment; plainness; severe simplicity.

austerity.ety: From Ancient Greek αὐστηρότης (austērótēs, “bitter, harsh”). Morphologically austere + -ity.

ex.en: He practices austerities almost like a monk.
ex.ja: 彼は僧侶に近い禁欲生活をしている。

ex.en: The fiscal austerity may lead to an overkill of the economy.
ex.ja: 緊縮財政政策は経済を冷やし過ぎることになるかもしれない。

ex.en: Fiscal austerity is considered to be an answer to the rampant inflation.
ex.ja: 激しいインフレに対処するには、緊縮財政が必要だと考えられている。

note.ja: austere（厳しい）+ -ity。ギリシャ語 austēros（渋い・厳しい）。「緊縮・簡素」。

Very; exceedingly; extremely; excessively.

awfully.ety:

From awful + -ly.

ex.en: Your new car looks awfully expensive to me.
ex.ja: あなたの新車はずいぶん高そうですね。

ex.en: We are awfully fed up with his long speech.
ex.ja: 私たちは彼の長話に全くあきあきしている。

ex.en: I'm awfully sorry that I was late.
ex.ja: 遅れまして、誠に申し訳ありません。

note.ja: awful（ひどい）+ -ly。「ひどく」→（口語）「とても」。

en: An arrangement or bunch of cut flowers; a nosegay.
A decoratively arranged bunch of something.

ex.en: He presented me with a bouquet of flowers.
ex.ja: 彼が花束をプレゼントしてくれたの。

ex.en: Tom gave a bouquet of flowers to Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーに花束をあげた。

ex.en: This wine has a good bouquet.
ex.ja: このワインは良い香りがする。

note.ja: フランス語 bouquet（小さな森・花束）から。bois（森）。「花束」→（ワインの）香り。

en: The state of being a candidate; candidateship.

ex.en: No one expected him to announce his candidacy again.
ex.ja: 彼がまた立候補するとは誰も予期していなかった。

note.ja: candidate（候補者）+ -cy。ラテン語 candidatus（白衣を着た人）。古代ローマの立候補者は白いトーガを着た。

en: To cut meat in order to serve it.
To shape to sculptural effect; to produce (a work) by cutting, or to cut (a material) into a finished work, especially with cuts that are…
The act of carving

carve.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ-der.
Proto-Germanic *kerbaną
Proto-West Germanic *kerban
Old English ċeorfan
Middle English kerven
English carve
From Middle English kerven, from Old English ceorfan, from Proto-West Germanic *kerban, from Proto-Germanic *kerbaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ- (“to scratch”). Cognate with West Frisian kerve, Dutch kerven, Low German karven, German kerben (“to notch”); also Old Prussian gīrbin (“number”), Old Church Slavonic жрѣбии (žrěbii, “lot, tallymark”), Ancient Greek γράφειν (gráphein, “to scratch, etch”).

ex.en: The host usually carves the roast at the table.
ex.ja: 普通はお客を招いた人が食卓で焼き肉を切り分けます。

ex.en: At times I confuse curve with carve.
ex.ja: 私は時々ＣｕｒｖｅとＣａｒｖｅを混同してしまう。

ex.en: At times I confuse "curve" with "carve".
ex.ja: 時々、ｃｕｒｖｅとｃａｒｖｅを間違えてしまう。

note.ja: 古英語 ceorfan（切る）から。「彫る・切り分ける」。

en: Any building used by a club for meetings or social activities.
A locker room and possibly associated rooms used by an athletic team.

ex.en: Hats aren't allowed to be worn inside the clubhouse.
ex.ja: クラブハウスの中で帽子を被ってはいけません。

note.ja: club + house。「クラブハウス」。

en: With a rough texture; not smooth.
Composed of large particles.

coarse.ety: Adjectival use of course that diverged in spelling in the 18th century. The sense developed from '(following) the usual course' (cf. of course) to 'ordinary, common' to 'lacking refinement', with 'not fine, granular' arising from its application to cloth. Compare the development of mean.

ex.en: He is coarse in manner.
ex.ja: 彼は態度が粗野だ。

ex.en: Her dress was made of coarse wool.
ex.ja: 彼女のドレスはきめの粗いウールでできていた。

ex.en: Her skin is coarse from years of working outdoors.
ex.ja: 彼女の肌は長年戸外で働いたのできめが粗くなっている。

note.ja: course（コース）の変化形。of course（普通の）→「ありふれた」→「粗い・下品な」。

en: Of, or relating to a college, or college students; collegial.
Of or relating to a collegium.
A high school.

collegiate.ety: From Middle English collegiate, from Medieval Latin collēgiātus (“colleague”), from collēgium (“community, group”).

note.ja: college + -iate。「大学の」。

en: Ordinary; not having any remarkable characteristics.
A platitude or cliché.
Something that is ordinary; something commonly done or occurring.
To make a commonplace book.
To enter in a commonplace book, or to reduce to general heads.

commonplace.ety: A calque of Latin locus commūnis, referring to a generally applicable literary passage, itself a calque of Ancient Greek κοινὸς τόπος (koinòs tópos).

ex.en: Space travel will be commonplace some time in the future.
ex.ja: 宇宙旅行はそのうち珍しくないものになるだろう。

ex.en: Translation features are becoming commonplace.
ex.ja: 翻訳機能が当たり前になっている。

ex.en: In my grandmother's lifetime, both telephones and computers have become commonplace.
ex.ja: 祖母が生きているうちに、電話もコンピューターも一般的なものとなった。

note.ja: common（ありふれた）+ place（場所・論点）。ラテン語 locus communis のなぞり。「ありふれたこと」。

en: In a confident manner; with confidence; with strong assurance; positively.

confidently.ety:

From confident + -ly.

note.ja: confident（自信のある）+ -ly。con + fidere（信頼する）。「自信をもって」。

en: Kept within close bounds; confined.
Forced; compelled.

ex.en: I was constrained to tell a lie.
ex.ja: 私はやむなく嘘をついた。

ex.en: I felt constrained to help her.
ex.ja: 私はどうしても彼女を助けなければならない気がした。

ex.en: We are constrained to and restrained from an action.
ex.ja: 我々は行動を強制されたり禁止されたりする。

note.ja: constrain（制約する）+ -ed。con + stringere（締める）。「制約された」。strict と同じ。

en: Encircling something (like a crown), especially with regard to the arteries or veins of the heart.
Any of the coronary vessels; a coronary artery or coronary vein.
A small bone in the foot of a horse.

note.ja: ラテン語 coronarius（冠の）から。corona（冠）。心臓を冠のように取り巻く「冠動脈の」。crown と同じ。

en: A bend; turn; curve; curvature; a flexure.
A bending of the knee; a genuflection.
To bend, or form into a hook.
To become bent or hooked.

crook.ety:
From Middle English croke, crok, from Old English *crōc (“hook, bend, crook”), from Proto-West Germanic *krōk, from Proto-Germanic *krōkaz (“bend, hook”), from Proto-Indo-European *greg- (“tracery, basket, bend”).
Cognate with Dutch kreuk (“a bend, fold, wrinkle”), Middle Low German kroke, krake (“fold, wrinkle”), Danish krog (“crook, hook”), Swedish krok (“crook, hook”), Icelandic krókur (“hook”).
Compare typologically Czech křivák (< křivý < Proto-Slavic *krivъ, whence also *krivьda).

ex.en: The weather is crook.
ex.ja: お天気が悪いね。

ex.en: In our society we find men of integrity along with crooks.
ex.ja: われわれの社会には、高潔な人もいれば、詐欺師もいる。

note.ja: 北欧語 krókr（かぎ）から。「曲がったもの」→ 曲がった心 →「悪党」。crooked と同じ。

en: A vine in the gourd family, Cucumis sativus.
The edible fruit of this plant, having a green rind and crisp white flesh.

cucumber.ety: From Middle English cucumer, cucumber, from Old French cocombre, ultimately from Latin cucumis, cucumerem (possibly through an Old Occitan intermediate). Probably of Pre-Italic substrate origin. First attested in the late 14c. Displaced native English earthapple (see which for more), which has since acquired other senses.

ex.en: She was right in the middle of cutting cucumbers.
ex.ja: 彼女はきゅうりを切っている最中だった。

ex.en: I was as cool as a cucumber.
ex.ja: 私は落ち着き払っていた。

ex.en: I was cool as a cucumber.
ex.ja: 私は落ち着き払っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 cucumis（キュウリ）から。

en: A small cake baked in a usually paper container shaped like a cup, often with icing on top.
A term of endearment.
To mash a cupcake at; to cover with cupcake.
To cover or be abundant with cake-like decorations such as frills.

ex.en: Are you going to eat that cupcake?
ex.ja: あのカップケーキ、食べるつもりなの？

ex.en: Are you going to eat those cupcakes?
ex.ja: あのカップケーキ、食べるつもりなの？

ex.en: Someone ate all my cupcakes.
ex.ja: 誰かが僕のカップケーキ全部食べちゃった。

note.ja: cup（カップ）+ cake。カップで量って作ったケーキ、またはカップ形の型で焼いたことから。

zh: 睡眠狀態的 /睡眠状态的

en: Inactive, sleeping, asleep, suspended.
In a sleeping posture; distinguished from couchant.
A crossbeam or joist.

dormant.ety: From Middle English, from Old French, from Latin dormiēns, present participle of dormiō (“to sleep”).

ex.en: Mt. Asama is now dormant.
ex.ja: 浅間山は今静止している。

note.ja: フランス語 dormir（眠る）の現在分詞。ラテン語 dormire。「休眠中の」。dormitory（寝室・寮）と同じ。

en: To copy or imitate, especially a person.
of a program or device: to imitate another program or device

emulate.ety: First attested in 1586; borrowed from Latin aemulātus, perfect active participle of Latin aemulor (“to rival, emulate”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

note.ja: ラテン語 aemulari（張り合う）から。「見習う・張り合う」→ 他の機械をまねて動く →「エミュレートする」。

en: To form a circle around; to encircle.
To include within its scope; to circumscribe or go round so as to surround; to enclose; to contain.

encompass.ety: From Middle English encompassen. By surface analysis, en- + compass.

ex.en: The optimal formula which would encompass all these factors has not been proposed.
ex.ja: これらの要素をすべて包含するような最良の公式はこれまでのところ提案されていない。

note.ja: en（中に）+ compass（円・範囲）。「範囲内に入れる」→「包含する」。

en: Provided or furnished with something.
Founded by an endowment.

ex.en: His daughter was endowed with beauty and grace.
ex.ja: 彼の娘は美しさと上品さに恵まれていた。

ex.en: She is endowed with a talent for music.
ex.ja: 彼女は生まれつき音楽の才能に恵まれている。

ex.ja: 貯金をしておくとはあなたは慎重でしたね。

ex.en: He is young, and yet he is prudent.
ex.ja: 彼は若い、それなのに分別がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 prudens（先を見通す）から。providens の短縮。「慎重な」。provide と同じ。

note.ja: revolve（回転する）+ -ing。「回転する」→ revolving door（回転ドア）。

To move like the undulating surface of a body of water; to undulate.
To propagate like a moving wave.

ex.ja: 風の水の面が波だった。

ex.ja: 右手に海のさざ波が見えてきたよ。

ex.ja: 石が池に波紋を描いた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「さざ波・波紋」→ ripple effect（波及効果）。

ex.ja: その悪い知らせを話した時、ロイはまじめな顔つきをした。

ex.en: They watched the solemn ceremony in the church with awe.
ex.ja: 彼らは教会内での厳粛な儀式を畏敬の念をもって見守った。

ex.en: The priest pretends to be solemn in public.
ex.ja: その聖職者は人前では真面目なふりをする。

en: Having plenty of space; roomy; capacious.

spacious.ety: From Middle English spacious, from Old French spacios, from Latin spatiōsus. By surface analysis, space + -ious.

ex.ja: 父は家族の居間を広くした。

ex.en: The room is spacious and light.
ex.ja: その部屋は広くて明るい。

ex.en: This house is very spacious.
ex.ja: この家はとても広い。

note.ja: space（空間）+ -ious。「広々とした」。

en: Of the essence or essential element of a thing.
Constituting the substance of content rather than its style, and thus always nontrivial.
Part of a text that carries the meaning, such as words and their ordering.

ex.ja: 頭と胴体の間に首がある。

note.ja: イタリア語 torso（茎・胴だけの彫像）から。ギリシャ語 thyrsos（杖）。「胴体」。

ex.ja: 星座は何ですか？

ex.ja: サミはレイラの星座を知りたかった。

en: The act of abandoning, or the state of being abandoned; total desertion; relinquishment.
The voluntary leaving of a person to whom one is bound by a special relation, as a wife, husband or child; desertion.

abandonment.ety: Borrowed from French abandonnement, from abandonner (“to abandon, relinquish”). abandonner was originally equivalent to mettre à bandon (“to leave to the jurisdiction, i.e. of another”), bandon being from Medieval Latin bandum, bannum (“order, decree, ban”). Equivalent to abandon + -ment. (See also English banns.)

note.ja: abandon（見捨てる）+ -ment。古フランス語 à bandon（支配下に）。「放棄」。

en: Hell; the bottomless pit; primeval chaos; a confined subterranean ocean.
A bottomless or unfathomed depth, gulf, or chasm; hence, any deep, immeasurable; any void space.

abyss.ety: From Middle English abissus, from Late Latin abyssus (“a bottomless gulf”), from Ancient Greek ἄβυσσος (ábussos, “bottomless”, from ἀ- (a-, “not”) + βυσσός (bussós, “deep place”)), from βυθός (buthós, “deep place”). Displaced native Old English neowolnes.

ex.ja: 一歩誤るとせんじんの谷だ。

ex.en: She was in an abyss of despair.
ex.ja: 彼女は絶望のどん底にあった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 abyssos（底なしの）から。a（否定）+ byssos（底）。「深淵」。

Increase by something added; that which is added; augmentation from without.
To make a record of (additions to a collection); to add (something) to a collection (usually a museum's or archive's collection).

ex.ja: 多くの入党者があった。

en: The crime of deliberately starting a fire with intent to cause damage.
To illegally set fire to; to burn down in a criminal manner.

arson.ety: From Anglo-Norman and Old French arson, from the verb ardoir, from Latin ardeō (“to burn”). Compare ardent.

en: A woman whose main employment is homemaking, maintaining the upkeep of her home and tending to household affairs; often, such a woman who…
The wife of a householder; the mistress of a family; the female head of a household.

housewife.ety: From Middle English houswyf, housewif, huswijf, equivalent to house + wife; a doublet of hussy, which it was long distinguished from and displaced due to gradual negative connotation (see Online Etymology Dictionary entry). Cognate with West Frisian húswiif, Dutch huiswijf, German Low German Huuswief, German Hausweib.

ex.en: I would hate to become just a housewife.
ex.ja: ただの主婦にはなりたくありません。

ex.en: Housewives have a hundred things to do.
ex.ja: 主婦にはすることが山ほどある。

ex.en: I think that my mother is the perfect housewife.
ex.ja: 私の母は主婦のかがみだと思う。

note.ja: house（家）+ wife（女性）。「主婦」。hussy（はすっぱ娘）は housewife が縮まった語。

en: Someone who practices hypocrisy, who pretends to hold beliefs, or whose actions are not consistent with their claimed beliefs.

hypocrite.ety: From Old French ypocrite (Modern French hypocrite), from Latin hypocrita, from Ancient Greek ὑποκριτής (hupokritḗs, “actor, hypocrite”), from ὑποκρίνομαι (hupokrínomai, “to answer, act, feign”). Displaced native Old English līċettere.

ex.en: We are not hypocrites in our sleep.
ex.ja: 我々の睡眠中は偽善者ではない。

ex.en: He went as far as to call you a hypocrite.
ex.ja: 彼は君のことを偽善者とまで言った。

ex.en: I'm not a hypocrite.
ex.ja: 僕は、偽善者なんかじゃない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hypokritēs（役者）から。「仮面をかぶった役者」→「偽善者」。hypocrisy と同じ。

en: The act of incorporating, or the state of being incorporated.
The union of different ingredients in one mass; mixture; combination; synthesis.

incorporation.ety: From Middle English incorporacioun, from Old French incorporacion, from Late Latin incorporatio. By surface analysis, incorporate + -ion.

ex.en: The articles of incorporation have finally been completed for our Digital Groove Club.
ex.ja: ついに我がデジタルグルーヴクラブの定款が完成しました。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ corp（体）+ or + ation。一つの体に組み込むこと →「法人化・合併・組み込み」。

en: Feeling or causing joy.

ex.en: We saw a joyful sight.
ex.ja: 私たちは楽しい光景を目にした。

ex.en: We were filled with joyful expectation.
ex.ja: 期待に胸を膨らませていた。

note.ja: joy（喜び）+ -ful。「喜びに満ちた」。

en: A sport played on a field between two opposing teams using sticks (crosses) and a ball, whereby one team defeats the other by scoring mor…

lacrosse.ety: Borrowed from Canadian French la crosse (“the stick”).

ex.en: I thought you didn't know anything about lacrosse.
ex.ja: あなたはラクロスについて何も知らないと思っていました。

ex.en: I thought that you didn't know anything about lacrosse.
ex.ja: あなたはラクロスについて何も知らないと思っていました。

note.ja: カナダのフランス語 la crosse（司教杖のような棒）から。

en: The milky sap of several trees that coagulates on exposure to air; used to make rubber.
An emulsion of rubber in water, used in adhesives and the like.

latex.ety: Borrowed from New Latin latex (“clear fluid which is part of a humour or bodily fluid”), a later use of Latin latex (“water; liquid, fluid”). Potentially a borrowing from Ancient Greek λᾰ́τᾰξ (lắtăx, “drop of wine”), reformed by analogy to other nouns in -ex. The semantic shift, however, from drop of wine to water is difficult to explain and may indicate that both words originated from a separate language. Perhaps from the same root as Proto-Celtic *latis (Old Irish laith (“liquid, beer”), Welsh llad (“beer”)) or Proto-Germanic *ladjō- (Old High German letto (“clay, loam”), Old Norse leðja (“m

ex.en: I transcribed the original mimeographed edition into LATEX.
ex.ja: ガリ版刷りの原書をLATEXで清書した。

note.ja: ラテン語 latex（液体）から。ゴムの木の乳液 →「ラテックス」。

en: Remaining; left behind; extra; odd; in reserve.
Something left behind; an excess or remainder.
Remaining after a meal is complete or eaten for a later meal or snack.

ex.en: Tom fed his leftovers to his dog.
ex.ja: トムは食べ残しを犬にやった。

ex.en: I fed the leftovers to my dog.
ex.ja: 私は食べ残しを犬にやった。

ex.en: Take the leftover food home with you.
ex.ja: 食べ残しはお持ち帰りください。

note.ja: left（残された）+ over。「残り物」。

en: The process of making something legal, the process to legalize, decriminalization.

legalization.ety: From legalize + -ation. Piecewise doublet of loyalization.

note.ja: legalize（合法化する）+ -ation。ラテン語 lex（法）。「合法化」。

en: Limited to a particular area; in a local vicinity only.
Having undergone localization.

ex.en: I'm glad we didn't go there because there were some localized heavy rain showers.
ex.ja: 局地的な大雨だったらしいけど、行かなくて正解だったよ。

note.ja: localize + -ed。「局所的な・現地化された」。

en: Any species of the extinct genus Mammuthus, of large, usually hairy, elephant-like mammals with long curved tusks and an inclined back, w…
Something very large of its kind.
Comparable to a mammoth in its size; very large, huge, gigantic.

mammoth.ety:
From obsolete Russian ма́мант (mámant), modern ма́монт (mámont), probably from a Uralic word, such as Proto-Mansi *mān-oŋt (“earth horn”). Possibly influenced by behemoth.
Adjectival use was popularized in the early 1800s by references to the Cheshire Mammoth Cheese presented to American paleontologist and president Thomas Jefferson.

ex.en: The author's verbiage produced a document of mammoth size and microscopic import.
ex.ja: 著者の冗漫なスタイルは膨大な書類を作り出したが、その内容は乏しい。

note.ja: ロシア語 mamont から。シベリアの言葉に由来するとされる。「マンモス」→「巨大な」。

ja: すばらしい（英国のつづり）

en: Exciting wonder or surprise; astonishing; wonderful.

marvellous.ety: First attested from 1300 as Middle English merveilous, from Old French merveillus, from merveille (“a wonder”) + -us. Doublet of merveilleux. See also marvel.

ex.en: This forum is marvellous.
ex.ja: このフォーラムは素晴らしいです。

note.ja: marvelous のイギリスのつづり。

en: A pairing of two things, people or teams, especially for a competition

ex.en: Everyone fell silent when they saw the tournament matchups.
ex.ja: トーナメントの組み合わせを見たら、みんな無言になった。

note.ja: match up（組み合わせる）の名詞化。「対戦（カード）」。

en: Mediocre; lackluster; unexceptional; uninspiring.
Apathetic; unenthusiastic.
A judgement marked by indifference; lack of impression.
Final question particle expressing skepticism.
A bleating sound, as that of a sheep or goat.

meh.ety:
Popularized by the American television show The Simpsons; first used on the show in the episode titled "Sideshow Bob Roberts" (1994).
Possibly ultimately from Yiddish מע (me, “so-so”). First attested in 1928, with usage as an interjection dated to 1992.

note.ja: 無関心を表す間投詞。2000年代に広まった。

zh: 調制解調器 /调制解调器

en: A device that encodes digital computer signals into analog telephone signals and vice versa, allowing computers to communicate over a pho…
To transmit by modem.

ex.en: The modem was built into the computer.
ex.ja: モデムはコンピューターの中に組み込まれた。

note.ja: modulator-demodulator（変調・復調器）の短縮。

en: A recurring or dominant element; an artistic theme.
A short melodic or lyrical passage that is repeated in several parts of a work.

motif.ety: From French motif (1848), with the meaning of "main idea or theme". Doublet of motive.

note.ja: フランス語 motif（動機）から。motive と同じ。「モチーフ・主題」。

en: A mass of oat plants (genus Avena, especially Avena sativa).
Seeds of an oat plant, especially prepared as food.

note.ja: 古英語 āte から。oatmeal（オートミール）。

en: Of or pertaining to an omen or to omens; being or exhibiting an omen; significant.
Specifically, giving indication of a coming ill; being an evil omen

ominous.ety: From Latin ōminōsus (“full of foreboding”), from ōmen (“forbidden fruit, omen”), from Old Latin osmen, of uncertain origin, with many origins proposed (see ōmen).

ex.en: The sky looks ominous. I wonder if it will rain.
ex.ja: 空が怪しい。雨が降るかな。

ex.en: Gradually, the weather became ominous.
ex.ja: だんだん天気が怪しくなってきた。

note.ja: omen（前兆）+ -ous。ラテン語 omen。「不吉な」。

en: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see open, -ness.
Accommodating attitude or opinion, as in receptivity to new ideas, behaviors, cultures, peoples, environments, experiences, etc., differe…

openness.ety: From Middle English *opennesse, from Old English openness (“openness, publicity”), equivalent to open + -ness. Cognate with Old High German offannussi (“disclosure, revelation, openness”).

ex.en: His openness is a very positive quality, although not without its drawbacks.
ex.ja: 彼の寛容さは、難点が無いわけではないが、とても良い性向である。

note.ja: open（開いた）+ -ness。「開放性・率直さ」。

en: that has undergone optimization

note.ja: optimize（最適化する）+ -ed。ラテン語 optimus（最善の）。optimist と同じ。

en: To hear something that was not meant for one's ears.

overhear.ety: From Middle English overheren, from Old English oferhīeran (“to overhear, hear, disobey, disregard, neglect”), equivalent to over- + hear. Cognate with Dutch overhoren (“to hear, hear about”), German überhören (“to not hear, ignore”), Danish overhøre (“to overhear”), Icelandic yfirheyra (“to hear”), Gothic *𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽 (*ufarhausjan, “to disregard, disobey”) (in 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌴𐌹𐌽𐍃 (ufarhauseins)).

ex.en: I overheard Tom and Mary talking about me.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーが私のこと話してるの聞いちゃったんだ。

ex.en: He overheard the conversation by accident.
ex.ja: 彼は偶然その会話を耳にした。

ex.en: They were afraid of being overheard.
ex.ja: 彼らは立ち聞きされるのを恐れた。

note.ja: over（越えて）+ hear。「ふと耳にする」。

en: Very large; especially of something larger than normal for its type.

oversized.ety:

From over- + sized.

note.ja: over（過度に）+ sized（大きさの）。「特大の」。

en: Having to do with the pope or the papacy.

papal.ety: From Middle English papal, from Old French papal and Medieval Latin pāpālis (“papal”).

note.ja: ラテン語 papalis（教皇の）から。papa（父）。pope と同じ。

en: A situation of serious and immediate danger.
Something that causes, contains, or presents danger.
To cause to be in danger; to imperil; to risk.

peril.ety: From Middle English peril, from Old French peril, from Latin perīculum. Doublet of periculum.

ex.en: They faced the peril of falling rocks.
ex.ja: 彼らは落石の危険にさらされた。

ex.en: Many wild animals are in peril of losing their lives.
ex.ja: 多くの野生動物の生命が危険にさらされている。

note.ja: ラテン語 periculum（試み・危険）から。experiri（試す）と同系。「危険」。perilous。

en: Able to be played.
Of a move, giving a reasonable result; able to be played without losing.
A character in a game who may be chosen as the player character.

en: A tiny opening in the skin.
By extension any small opening or interstice, especially one of many, or one allowing the passage of a fluid.
To study meticulously; to go over again and again.
To meditate or reflect in a steady way.

pore.ety: From Middle English pore, from Old French pore, from Latin porus, from Ancient Greek πόρος (póros, “passage”). Displaced native English sweat hole from Middle English swet hole, which might have been a reformation of Old English swātþȳrel (literally “sweat hole”), which competed with līcþēote (literally “body pipe”).

ex.en: Witch hazel tightens pores without drying skin.
ex.ja: ウィッチヘーゼルは、乾燥させずに毛穴を引き締めます。

ex.en: I left Jeremy poring over his notes for his first accountancy exam tomorrow.
ex.ja: ジェレミは彼の会計士の一次試験のためノートを熱心に勉強していたよ。

note.ja: 「毛穴」はギリシャ語 poros（通り道）から。「熟読する」は中英語 pouren からで別語。
